entries.what_happened: The family is a single manuscript, 'A singular normal affine surface with free tangent sheaf'. Its Theorem 1 (thm:main) claims that there exist a finitely generated normal integral C-algebra A of Krull dimension two and a maximal ideal m of A with Der_C(A) ≅ A⊕A (free of rank two) and A_m not regular. The argument has two steps. (1) Proposition 'analytic-counterexample' builds a normal complex surface germ (X,x), smooth off x, with free holomorphic tangent sheaf of rank two. It takes a smooth genus-21 curve C with normal bundle L⁻¹, deg L = 10, L⁴ ≅ K_C; prescribes finite jets of two vector fields on a neighbourhood of C by finitely many holomorphic flows; glues these to a Hausdorff surface neighbourhood Y of C; lifts the jets holomorphically using vanishing of H¹ on the ideal filtration; and contracts C to x by Grauert's criterion. The text gives C² = −10, canonical discrepancy −5 for C, and p_g ≥ 33 (Remark 'invariants'). (2) Proposition 'algebraization' produces an affine normal A with the same completed local ring as (X,x) at the marked point, a principal affine neighbourhood on which Der_C(A) ≅ A^d with d = 2, and smoothness away from that point. The proof uses a finite-determinacy lemma with a relation matrix, which the paper proves itself, together with Artin approximation over a henselization.
entries.delivers: Disproves the statement as listed, in its affine form. The claim is a normal affine complex surface Spec A whose coordinate ring has free derivation module Der_C(A) ≅ A⊕A, and which is singular at m because A_m is not regular. The manuscript says the result 'disproves the Lipman–Zariski conjecture in characteristic zero'. Its formulation matches the list: Der_C(A) is Hom_A(Ω¹_{A/C}, A), the hypothesis is freeness of the whole module, and the conclusion (smoothness) fails at a closed point. The introduction states the conjecture with 'locally free tangent sheaf'. Global freeness is a stronger hypothesis than local freeness, so the same example refutes that form too. The text also gives the analytic germ (the complex-space version) and the local ring A_m, whose derivations are free (Der_C(T) ≅ T^d in the proof). The text states that Spec A can be chosen smooth away from m. Normality of A is consistent with Lipman's theorem, which the introduction cites as showing that free derivations force normality.
entries.remains: If the claim holds, the listed statement is refuted and no part of it stays open. Not addressed by the text: the generalisation with reflexive p-forms; graded variants (the text remarks only that Hochster's graded theorem excludes getting this example from a positively graded cone); and higher dimensions. The introduction cites van Straten and Steenbrink as proving the isolated-singularity case in dimension at least three, so any higher-dimensional counterexample must have non-isolated singularities, and the manuscript does not treat that. No explicit equations for A are given.
entries.direction: disproves the conjecture (affine, dimension two, characteristic zero)
entries.object: Yes, but not explicit. Spec A is never written down. It is produced by existence arguments: a general genus-21 curve C on P¹×P¹ (Bertini and 'general' parameter conditions), a gluing of finitely many holomorphic flows, Grauert's contraction, and Artin approximation over a henselization followed by an étale shrinking. The analytic germ (X,x) is likewise non-explicit. Several choices are made by 'sufficiently general' or 'sufficiently small' conditions without explicit values.
entries.conditional_on: None for the main theorem beyond published results the proof cites (Grauert's contraction and formal-function theorems, Artin's approximation theorem, Cartan's Theorem B, Serre's GAGA comparison, Cutkosky's excellence result). No other manuscript in the family is needed for the main theorem. Two corollaries depend on external results: the log-Kodaira-dimension corollary (algebra:log-kodaira) depends on Biswas–Gurjar–Kolte 2014, Theorem 0.1(1); the derivation-blowup corollary (algebra:derivation-blowups) depends on Villamayor's description as recalled in Barajas–Chávez-Martínez–Romano-Velázquez (arXiv:2510.07607), §1.6, Theorem 1.17. Neither is needed for the main claim.
entries.doubts: (a) The algebraization proof states that Der_C(T)⊗T̂ ≅ Der^cont(T̂,T̂) ≅ T̂^d 'is an equality obtained from finite presentations; it does not identify ordinary algebraic differentials of a power-series ring with its continuous differentials'. Freeness descent passes through this identity, and the text itself flags the distinction. (b) The finite-determinacy lemma with a relation matrix is proved in the paper rather than cited. The text presents it as a variant of Hironaka's and Artin's methods, 'including fixed estimates that avoid a complete-intersection hypothesis'. Its proof is an iterative improvement argument whose constants are fixed abstractly (by Artin–Rees), with no explicit values. (c) Several verifications are compressed. Closedness of the gluing graphs ends with 'Possible fiber boundaries cause no difficulty'. The order-two obstruction is settled by 'the following calculation evaluates all four' tests. Higher-order steps are given as formulas without all intermediate expansions. (d) Several existence steps rest on genericity ('general', 'sufficiently small', Bertini) and give no explicit parameters. (e) The introduction cites Bergner and Graf's inequality p_g − g − b ≤ 2 without stating what it implies. The claim that the example lies 'beyond' that criterion depends on reading it as a smoothness criterion. I found no inconsistency between the abstract, the introduction, Theorem 1 and the proof sections I read.

entries.what_happened: The manuscript ('A singular normal affine surface with free tangent sheaf') says nothing about rings of differential operators, D(V), or Nakai's conjecture. A search of its build sources finds no mention of either. Its only claim in this area is the Lipman–Zariski counterexample in the entry above: a normal affine surface A with Der_C(A) ≅ A⊕A and A_m not regular.
entries.delivers: No claim about the Nakai hypothesis or conclusion. The manuscript does not show that the ring of differential operators of A, or of any other variety, is generated by its order-one operators. The family bears on Nakai only through the implication that the problem's context cites, namely that Nakai's conjecture implies Zariski–Lipman (Becker; Rego). If that implication holds, refuting Zariski–Lipman as this family does would also refute Nakai's conjecture. The manuscript neither states nor uses that route, and it does not verify the Nakai hypothesis for A. So the family does not settle Nakai on its own argument.
entries.remains: All of the Nakai problem as far as these manuscripts go: whether any singular complex variety, including the constructed A, has its ring of differential operators generated by derivations, and the order-n form for n ≥ 2 quoted in the problem context.
entries.direction: no direct direction; refutes Zariski–Lipman, which bears on Nakai only via the cited implication
entries.conditional_on: Bearing on Nakai requires the implication Nakai ⇒ Zariski–Lipman, which the manuscript neither states nor proves. I did not check the cited source (arXiv:2604.24508) and did not search for it. It also requires that the ring of differential operators of the constructed A, or of a variety derived from it, is generated by derivations, which the text does not address.
entries.doubts: The manuscript does not discuss differential operators at all, so nothing in the text checks the Nakai hypothesis for any variety. Any reading that counts this family as refuting Nakai depends entirely on the external implication.
